_comment: aowl.basement -- Escape From My Basement: the always-in-raid RPG backend. OFF by default, for three separate reasons, each of which is a thing you should agree to before it happens: (1) it spawns subprocesses (whisper for speech-in, piper for speech-out) and loads hundreds of megabytes of model; (2) it writes a PERSISTENT WORLD into the mod store and keeps advancing it on a timer, so it changes state while nobody is looking; (3) with llmEngine set to anything but 'builtin' it makes outbound HTTP calls to a paid API. Nothing here is read off disk by the mod itself -- the host serves these through setting(). GET /aowlspt/basement/status to see which engine resolved to which absolute path and whether it is actually there, and GET /aowlspt/basement/selfcheck for the nine falsifiable checks of DESIGN.md §9.
_preset: Which world to generate: an id under data/presets/. Shipped: warlords (four armed gangs, land grabs, enslavement is a real outcome), quiet_apocalypse (few people, scarcity, deals matter), cult_of_the_reactor (one cult, one resistance), the_long_road (convoys and escorts), sandbox (neutral everything, for testing). Write your own by dropping a JSON file in beside them.
_seed: 0 means PICK ONE from the wall clock, so two worlds made a second apart differ. The seed actually used is stored in the world and reported by /status -- a seed you cannot read back is not a seed, it is a coincidence. Any non-zero value is deterministic: the same seed and the same preset generate a byte-identical world (selfcheck 1 asserts exactly that, and asserts a different seed differs).
_worldPrompt: Empty = the preset's own prompt. This string is the top of every system prompt: what this world IS. It is the single highest-leverage thing to edit.
_engines: Each stage dispatches on these strings. llmEngine: builtin | anthropic | openai | llamacpp | none. sttEngine: whisper-server | none. ttsEngine: piper | kokoro | chatterbox | client | sapi | none. kokoro = Kokoro-82M on the CPU (onnx, ~1.3 s per sentence on this i9, MEASURED 2026-09-07), chatterbox = Resemble Chatterbox on CUDA with voice CLONING from data/voices/<stem>.wav (~3.5 s per sentence on the RTX 2060 SUPER, MEASURED), client = no wav from here, the game-side plugin synthesises from the say segment's text + voiceSpec. Both local servers are started by this backend on first use (detached, via PowerShell Start-Process) when /health does not answer; tools/kokoro/setup.ps1 and tools/chatterbox/setup.ps1 install them OUTSIDE the repo under %LOCALAPPDATA%/aowlspt/<engine>/.
_ttsAsync: true (default): a kokoro/chatterbox/openai-tts sentence is synthesised OFF the tick. curl is spawned detached; the local servers write the wav atomically and then an empty `<wav>.done` marker, and for the cloud engine cmd writes the marker after curl exits 0; the tick collects it and emits the `say` segment then, in per-person order. MEASURED 2026-09-07 with it false: ttsSegment ran inside onTick's withModLock, one kokoro sentence blocked EVERY route for ~1.3 s, and a 5-sentence turn timed an /events long-poll out. piper and sapi are subprocesses we run to completion for their exit status -- there is no endpoint to leave a marker -- so they stay synchronous and /status ttsAsync.note says so rather than claiming async for every engine.
_ttsTimeoutMs: The bounded wait for a wav. After it the segment is emitted WITHOUT audio and its ttsNote says the wait was given up on, so the client shows the subtitle instead of the turn going silent forever. The request is still watched afterwards, and a wav that lands late is still committed to the cache, so the same sentence is instant next time.
_spawnMode: How every detached child (curl for the LLM stream and for TTS, the kokoro/chatterbox/whisper servers) is started. "process" = CreateProcessW called DIRECTLY with bInheritHandles=FALSE, MEASURED 2026-09-07 at ~1 ms. "powershell" = Start-Process, MEASURED at 197-204 ms idle and 300-500 ms on the live sidecar; kept as the fallback. TWO candidates were tried and REJECTED ON EVIDENCE: `cmd /c start` hung our own runCmd read for the child's ENTIRE lifetime (10110 ms with a 10 s child; redirecting the child's streams gave 10112 ms and a new console 10218 ms) because the grandchild inherits the pipe runCmd made for that very call; and std/osproc.startProcess hardcodes bInheritHandles=TRUE, after which four detached whisper-server children held the stdout pipe of the process reading US and tools/basement_check.py hung forever, after the simulator had already exited.
_cloudSpeech: The `openai`, `openai-whisper` and `openai-tts` engines are really "any OpenAI-COMPATIBLE endpoint". Groq serves all three shapes at https://api.groq.com/openai/v1 and is far faster -- MEASURED 2026-09-07: chat openai/gpt-oss-120b answered a full in-character reply in 0.49-0.56 s (vs ~4 s on gpt-4o-mini), whisper-large-v3-turbo transcribed a 42 KB push-to-talk wav in 0.53 s round trip, and canopylabs/orpheus-v1-english returned a 119110-byte RIFF wav in 0.63 s. THE KEY IS NEVER WRITTEN HERE: openAiKeyEnv/sttKeyEnv/ttsKeyEnv NAME an environment variable and the value is read from the process environment, so switching provider changes which variable is read, never where a secret lives. Every default below points at the LOCAL engines; the sidecar config is what selects Groq.
_openAiExtraJson: A raw JSON fragment WITHOUT the surrounding braces, spliced into every chat request. Empty by default because real OpenAI 400s on an unknown field. For Groq openai/gpt-oss-120b set it to "reasoning_effort":"low" -- MEASURED 2026-09-07: without it the model spends max_tokens on a `reasoning` field first, so at max_tokens 80 the spoken content came back EMPTY and at 120 it was cut off mid-word (finish_reason length); with it the reasoning fell from 487 to 57 characters and the whole reply landed in 488 ms.
_ttsModel: For ttsEngine openai-tts. canopylabs/orpheus-v1-english on Groq; the per-person voice comes from data/voices.json `orpheus` (daniel, tara, leah, jess, leo, dan, mia, zac, zoe). Orpheus honours inline emotive cues like <laugh>; there is NO documented shout tag -- <yell>/<shout> are read as literal text and SPOKEN -- so a yell segment is upper-cased with a terminal ! and that is a weak effect, stated rather than claimed.
_llmEngineNote: 'builtin' is the ontology's fallback row -- a TEMPLATE RESPONDER, NOT A LANGUAGE MODEL -- and it says so in the notes of every reply it produces. It is the default because it is the only tier that works on this machine today: ANTHROPIC_API_KEY and OPENAI_API_KEY are both unset here, and a full-disk sweep found no .gguf. Set llmEngine to 'anthropic' AND put a key in the environment to get a real model.
_anthropicModel: Used when llmEngine=anthropic. The key comes from the ANTHROPIC_API_KEY environment variable and NEVER from this file -- EscapeFromMyBasement hardcoded a live key into its plugin and shipped it inside the DLL. The request carries the stable part of the prompt with cache_control so provider prompt caching applies; usage.cache_read_input_tokens is reported on /status so a silent cache invalidation is visible instead of merely expensive.
_maxTokens: Cap on a single spoken reply. A 1-3 sentence line does not need more.
_llmStreaming: true (default): the model's reply is spoken SENTENCE BY SENTENCE while it is still being written. curl is spawned DETACHED with the SSE going to a file, the backend tick parses the new bytes every tickMs, and each completed sentence goes straight to TTS and out as a `say` segment; POST /say and a push-to-talk/chunk final answer immediately with {ok, turnId, streaming:true} and the segments arrive on /events, the last carrying final:true. MEASURED 2026-09-07 before this existed: ~4 s of silence on gpt-4o-mini before the first spoken word. Set it to false for the old synchronous shape -- identical text, one reply, after the whole response has arrived -- which is what the deterministic offline checks assert against. Only the anthropic and openai engines have a streaming wire format here; llamacpp and builtin stay synchronous and say so.
_maxTurnsInFlight: How many streaming turns may be running at once. A turn beyond the bound is answered SYNCHRONOUSLY (with a note saying why) rather than queued behind another person's sentence.
_turnTimeoutMs: A streaming turn whose SSE never ends is closed after this long: the ontology's fallback line is spoken and the note says TIMED OUT. Without it a dead connection is indistinguishable from a short reply.
_debugTickRoute: Adds POST /aowlspt/basement/tick, which runs the backend tick N times. The simulator runs every route BEFORE it runs a tick, so this is the only way to drive the streaming parser offline. OFF by default; a game client should never call it.
_llmFakeStreamFile: TEST ONLY. A fixture SSE file that stands in for curl entirely -- no key is read and no process is started; the poller reveals llmFakeChunkBytes of it per tick so 'a sentence was spoken BEFORE the stream ended' is observable offline. llmFakeStreamStall reveals the first chunk and then nothing, which is the input that makes the turnTimeoutMs path fire.
_maxTurns: How many lines of the conversation go back into the prompt, on top of the bounded [REMEMBER:] lines a person chose to keep.
_toolsDir: Holds whisper/ and piper/. These are EscapeFromMyBasement's, already downloaded by its tools/Setup-EFMyBasement.ps1 (MEASURED present at D:/SPT/disabled_mods/EscapeFromMyBasement/tools on 2026-09-06) -- this mod reuses them rather than fetching 230 MB again. The four overrides below default from it; set one to point an engine somewhere else.
_kokoro: kokoroUrl: where the kokoro server answers (POST /tts, GET /health). kokoroRoot: the setup.ps1 root holding venv/, kokoro-v1.0.onnx, voices-v1.0.bin and server.py; empty = %LOCALAPPDATA%/aowlspt/kokoro. kokoroExe: the python to spawn it with; empty = <kokoroRoot>/venv/Scripts/python.exe.
_chatterbox: chatterboxUrl / chatterboxRoot / chatterboxExe: the same three for the CUDA cloning server (root default %LOCALAPPDATA%/aowlspt/chatterbox). voicesDir: the folder of <stem>.wav reference voices it clones from; empty = data/voices beside the mod. The three shipped wavs there are PLACEHOLDERS made with piper and Windows SAPI -- drop real ~10 s recordings in and point data/voices.json tags at their stems.
_curlExe: The only HTTP client available to a nimony mod. Windows ships one in System32.
_workDir: Where recorded and spoken .wav files land. Empty = %TEMP%.
_cacheDir: Empty = mods/basement/data/cache beside the mod, so it survives a restart. Holds brain.json (the line cache) and tts/ (one wav per spoken sentence).
_ontologyMinConfidence: How sure the intent classifier has to be before its template answer is used instead of falling through to the LLM. 0 means AUTOMATIC and depends on the engine: 0.6 with llmEngine=builtin|none (the table is the only responder there is), 0.9 otherwise, where the table answers only dead-certain greet/insult repeats and everything else goes to the model. Any non-zero value here is taken as deliberate and used as-is. Every ontology reply is marked tier:'ontology' so nobody mistakes it for a model.
_pushToTalk: POST /aowlspt/basement/speech/ptt {session,state:down|up} moves speech CAPTURE to the backend, because on aowlspt the client cannot capture at all -- EFT holds the microphone exclusively, which is why EscapeFromMyBasement ships a standalone winmm recorder.exe (aowl.voice reuses it for the same reason). recorderExe: empty = <toolsDir>/recorder/recorder.exe. pttMaxSeconds: the recorder is spawned with this bound and CANNOT be interrupted from here -- its stop protocol is a line on stdin and a detached spawn has no stdin, and the alternative (an inherited pipe) is a hang aowl.voice measured twice -- so key-up finalises over whatever is on disk at that moment and says so in its reply. While it records, the tick feeds the GROWING file (taking the data chunk's OFFSET, never its size field: the recorder writes the RIFF sizes only when it exits) so heard.partial events appear progressively.
_sttPartialMs: How much NEW audio must arrive before whisper is run again on the session buffer and a heard.partial is emitted. A partial is NEVER fed to the brain -- whisper's partials are unstable, measured in aowl.voice.
_encounters: leashM: how far a prisoner may stray from their captor before it is an escape attempt (the client enforces it, the backend re-checks it from player_moved, and the attempt is journaled whether or not the player gets away). noticeM: how far a person notices the player. threatM: how close is close enough to be a threat.
_hearing: WHO CAN HEAR A LINE. hearSpeakM: how far a normal speaking voice carries (25 m). hearYellM: how far a SHOUT carries (70 m). Between the two, a line is REWRITTEN as a shout -- the ontology row's `yell` variant when it has one, otherwise the first sentence, shortened and upper-cased -- and goes out as mode:"yell" with voiceSpec.yell:true so the TTS engine can actually shout it. Beyond hearYellM NOTHING is emitted: the person's memory records that they saw the player and could not be heard, and say.suppressed is journaled, because a line dropped without a trace is indistinguishable from a broken state machine. The distance is always the CLIENT's (player_seen.distanceM, player_aimed_at.distanceM, or npc_moved vs player_moved); a distance nobody has reported is treated as AUDIBLE and every such segment says so in hearingNote -- refusing to speak on missing data would silently mute the whole mod.
_bystanderReactChance: The user, 2026-09-07: "everyone in the vicinity replies even if I can't hear their reply -- that's not good". A push-to-talk final now answers EXACTLY the addressee. Anyone else within hearSpeakM of the player may throw in ONE short bark from data/ontology.json's `bystander` table -- never an LLM turn, never a reply -- with this probability and bystanderCooldownMs between them. Every one is marked reaction:true on the wire, which is how selfcheck 22 tells a reaction from a reply.
_chatterLevel: How much people speak on their OWN initiative: 0 off entirely, 1 normal, 2 talkative (every trigger's rate limit is halved). The triggers are first_sight (the first time they see you this raid), approach (you close 10+ m on them within 3 s), linger (10 s within 8 m without talking), hurt (they are shot), saw_death (someone dies within 30 m of them), combat_taunt (every 8-15 s while fighting, yelled), push (you close 15+ m in 3 s -- a sprint), bystander (overhearing). Each has its own switch below, and every line comes from the `barks` table in data/ontology.json, never from code.
_barkCooldownMs: How long a person stays barked-out after a threat line. MEASURED 2026-09-07: the client reports player_aimed_at every tick the crosshair rests on someone, so without this window every tick re-fired the threat transition -- one sentence repeated forever and ~40 un-acked npc.attack directives in two minutes. Inside the window the ticks are COUNTED (the journal row carries suppressedAimTicks) and nothing is emitted.
_stream: streamMax: the size of the in-memory directive ring. directiveTtlSeconds: how long a directive that needs an ack waits before it is journaled as directive.dropped -- that is the failure path announcing itself, not a retry. maxWaitMs: the cap on GET /events?wait=. HONESTY: that wait is a BOUNDED POLL on the request thread, not a parked socket, because the mod SDK exposes no sleep or condition variable; every /events reply says which mechanism it used and how long it actually waited.
_tick: tickMs: how often the backend advances the sim, steps escorts, and expires un-acked directives. saveEveryTicks: how many ticks between automatic saves (0 = only on demand). The world keeps moving while you are in the menu -- that is the point of it.
_sim: simMaxCatchUpHours caps the catch-up that runs when a world is loaded after the process was not running -- without a cap, a world left for a month would try to simulate a month at boot. simMoveEveryMinutes is how much world time passes between movement decisions. ambushChance is the per-opportunity chance that being near a hostile faction's dangerous place turns into a group.spawn.
_autoRaidRequests: NOT DONE, and off for that reason: /spawn emits the mod-bus event basement.raid.request {map,x,y,z}, and mods/autoraid is the intended consumer but does not subscribe to it yet (DESIGN.md §10). Turning this on today emits an event nothing listens to.
_bridge: THE CLIENT HALF (aowlspt only). Read by the same DLL when it is loaded into the game. It does nothing unless bridgeEnabled is true AND the host flags hostHttp and hostPlayWav are on (both default OFF in aowlspt-host.json); every refusal is logged once, by name.
_bridgeBackendUrl: Where the backend answers. https:// is refused by the host verb; the host allowlist is loopback only.
_bridgePollWaitMs: How long /events may hold the request open, clamped 0..25000 (the backend's own cap).
_bridgePttKey: Push-to-talk key. NOTHING READS IT TODAY (no host verb reports key state); drive PTT with the bus event basement.ptt {state:down|up}.
_bridgeSpawnOnMenu: At MENU, ask GET /spawn and hand the map to mods/autoraid (autoraid.arm). Never re-arms while a request is unanswered or the phase is not MENU.
